items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: He was Creole, yes. He was Creole and he was from Lake Charles.

ctx.x: And I think you also said before that Snake Griffin was a Creole, right?

He was Creole, yes. He was Creole and he was from Lake Charles. In later years he went up -- he came out to California as a matter of fact, and I don't know now if he's still around or not, but he did come out to California. He was a part of this orchestra, part of the Imperial Orchestra, and then he went into the Southern Rhythm Boys.
You mentioned earlier that you had learned from your father how to play guitar, violin and mandolin. Did you ever use any of that knowledge in any of the bands you played in?

items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Then we had Snake Griffin... He was a part of this orchestra, part of the Imperial Orchestra

ctx.x: He played drums. Eldridge Joe. Then we had Snake Griffin. Snake was a saxophone player, a tenor saxophone player. We also had, from Lake Charles we had -- let's see, Eldridge Joe, Snake Griffin -- oh, from Apaloosa, Louisiana we had a marvelous saxophone player by the name of Lawrence Emerson who later sort of got away from the music business and became an educator. He was the principal of a school. I think he just retired a couple of years (ago). Down in the little city of Apaloosa, Louisiana. And then I…
I think you mentioned on the earlier tape that Eldridge Joe later played with what orchestra, Don Abbott?
